scope.description: Follower main goroutine handling a valid InstallSnapshot RPC while raftState.lastLogIndex is above the incoming snapshot index and the injected LogStore implements MonotonicLogStore with IsMonotonic() true.
assumptions: The InstallSnapshot request is legal: supported snapshot version, term not older than currentTerm, size matching the streamed bytes.
The LogStore faithfully implements the LogStore interface and reports IsMonotonic() true, so the install path calls removeOldLogs.
The leader continues to replicate from snapshotIndex+1 after a successful install (as sendLatestSnapshot does).
excluded: Non-monotonic LogStores, where installSnapshot calls compactLogs and keeps trailing entries
The case where the cached last log index is at or below the snapshot index, which the max() in getLastEntry/getLastIndex already covers
Consensus safety or data loss: the discarded entries are uncommitted

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: skipStartup is set and only the FSM goroutine is started, so the install handler runs without the main loop; installSnapshot's restore step therefore reaches the real FSM goroutine and the FSM is a no-op stub that ignores the snapshot bytes.
The single-voter configuration is installed directly rather than bootstrapped, so the handler's peer-set update and log reset run without real peers.
The snapshot payload is three arbitrary bytes with a matching Size; the content is irrelevant because the stub FSM performs no restore work.

plan_uncertainties: The check uses one follower without the main loop and a single-voter configuration; it establishes the local recovery responsibility, not a cluster-wide consequence.
The FSM is a no-op stub, so only raft's own bookkeeping (cached log identity, log store contents, append acceptance) is exercised.
Only the monotonic-store branch is instantiated; the non-monotonic compactLogs branch is a recorded alternative.
grounding_unresolved: Whether a legal history produces a cached last log index above the leader's chosen snapshot index.
Whether the rejection loop terminates through a later successful store or repeats with the cache never updated.
